title: Doing Business In cuba - Chandrawat & Partners

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuba comprises the main island plus 4,195 islands, islets, and cays.
facts.quote: It comprises the eponymous main island as well as 4,195 islands, islets, and cays.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuba has about 10 million inhabitants.
Chandrawat & Partners states that over 7,000 new private businesses have opened in Cuba since 2021.
facts.quote: with over 7,000 new private businesses opening since 2021.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuban residents, defined as those present more than 182 days, are taxed on global income, while non-residents are taxed only on local income.
facts.quote: Residents (present >182 days) are taxed on global income, while non-residents are taxed only on local income.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that progressive tax rates for self-employment in Cuba can reach up to 50%.
facts.quote: Progressive tax rates for self-employment can reach up to 50%.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuban corporate tax (CIT) is generally 30%.
facts.quote: Generally taxed at 30%, but foreign-owned companies often face a 35% rate

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that foreign-owned companies in Cuba often face a corporate tax rate of 35%.
facts.quote: but foreign-owned companies often face a 35% rate, and new, approved investments may be exempt for the first eight years.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that new, approved investments in Cuba may be exempt from corporate tax for the first eight years.
facts.quote: new, approved investments may be exempt for the first eight years.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuban sales tax is 2% on wholesale.
facts.quote: Sales Tax: 2% on wholesale, 10% on retail and services.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuban sales tax is 10% on retail and services.
facts.quote: Sales Tax: 2% on wholesale, 10% on retail and services.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuban social security and labor force contributions are often around 14%.
facts.quote: Social Security/Labor Force: Contributions are required, often around 14%.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that private MSMEs (MIPYMES or PYMEs) in Cuba are small and medium-sized companies with up to 100 employees, allowed since 2021.
facts.quote: Small and medium-sized private companies (up to 100 employees) allowed since 2021, often acting as limited liability companies (SRLs).

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that a Cuban joint venture company (Empresa Mixta) must be created by at least one Cuban partner and one foreign partner.
facts.unit: minimum Cuban partner and foreign partner each
facts.quote: this is a corporation (SA) created by at least one Cuban partner and one foreign partner.

facts.fact: Chandrawat & Partners states that Cuba's Foreign Investment Law 118 provides a legal framework including investment protection and the ability to use international arbitration.
facts.quote: Foreign Investment Law 118 provides a legal framework, including investment protection and the ability to utilize international arbitration for dispute resolution.
